Chromatin means eukaryotic DNA-histone complex; the textbook defines chromosome as inside the nucleus. Bacteria lack histone chromatin (archaea have histones). Eukaryote-only premise applied to prokaryotes.
Depolarisation opens Na+ channels, Na+ enters: a positive-feedback loop (action potential). Link a student may not make alone.
Derivation unsound: 'these atoms' in the two premises are different atoms (anaphora). NADPH holds no glucose part; NADPH hydrogen goes TO sugar in the Calvin cycle.

Loop claim: one route is insulin -> low glucose -> more glucagon -> more glucose -> more insulin, but the net effect of insulin on insulin is negative (it lowers glucose, which lowers insulin). Same system also derives the opposite sign. Autocrine insulin signalling in beta cells is a separate, debated story.
Negative premise is about prokaryote chromosomes (no nuclear membrane); inherited down to eukaryotes where it is false. Startling if true; negation inheritance error.

Premise says plasma membrane regulates passage and blocks some substances; 'inhibits transport' is a poor reading, and sits oddly beside R065 (it carries out transport). Selective barrier, not an inhibitor.
Same error as R068. GO 'digestion' is gut digestion; macrophages fight pathogens (and digest them inside the cell, a different process). Commensal gut bacteria are not their target in health.
